A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CRV research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original verification experiments on Boolean, Arithmetic, and GSM8K tasks, together with ablations, annotation validation, and causal intervention case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds evaluations of an MLP probe and a CRV classifier trained on the combined training sets.

M1.justification: The proposed CRV pipeline retains the same transcoders, attribution graph construction and pruning, graph features, and gradient-boosting classifier. The added probe is a comparator, while combined training introduces an experimental condition without changing the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Boolean, Arithmetic, and GSM8K tasks, plus RedPajama-V2 and LMSYS-Chat-1M for transcoder training experiments. Combining existing training sets does not introduce additional data or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds a two-layer MLP Probe to the main comparison in Table 1. All earlier black-box and gray-box baselines remain, as do the alternative graph-feature classifiers in v1 Table 16, now v2 Table 18.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 adds a condition that trains one CRV classifier on the union of all three training sets and evaluates it on each task. The new MLP baseline also introduces validation-based hyperparameter selection. Existing splits, metrics, and retained experimental settings are unchanged; Appendix C.3 provides additional metric documentation.

E4.justification: The cross-domain analysis now tests whether one jointly trained classifier can accommodate different tasks' error patterns. Existing difficulty tests, feature-family ablations, transcoder fine-tuning and attribution-position analyses, visualizations, and both causal intervention cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same independent t-tests and Cohen's d for feature distributions, and kappa and percentage agreement for annotation validation. v2 introduces no new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practices.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds MLP Probe results, including AUROCs of 53.63, 54.41, and 56.02 for Boolean, Arithmetic, and GSM8K. Table 2 adds combined-training AUROCs of 65.18, 90.51, and 70.62, with accompanying AUPR and FPR@95 results. It also corrects in-domain GSM8K FPR@95 from 79.16 to 79.61, matching Table 1. The pooled-training scores concern a new condition; retained main CRV scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal problem formulation is unchanged. New Appendix C.3 states standard formulas for the already-used AUROC, AUPR, and FPR@95 metrics; it does not introduce new theoretical results, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, main scientific contribution statements, and conclusion retain the claims that computational graphs reveal predictive, domain-specific error signatures and support targeted causal interventions. The revised resource-release wording changes availability claims without redefining the scientific contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 moves beyond emphasizing failed zero-shot transfer and proposing diverse training as future work. It now interprets combined-training results as evidence that task-specific error patterns can coexist within one classifier, with possible beneficial transfer to GSM8K. Appendix E's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 promises dataset and transcoder release; v2 states their release and supplies a CRV repository link. Appendix C.2 adds the MLP probe's search grid and selected configurations, while C.3 documents metric computation and scikit-learn usage. These are additional access and reproducibility disclosures; repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds Venhoff et al. (2025) on latent reasoning algorithms and Lee et al. (2025) on self-verification circuits. These additions broaden the immediate research context while retaining CRV's original novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the cross-domain discussion, expands baseline documentation, and inserts an evaluation-metrics subsection, renumbering subsequent Appendix C subsections. Affiliation, correspondence, and bibliography formatting edits are also limited; the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 gain rows, and new Tables 16–17 present MLP hyperparameters. Existing displays are retained, with local spacing changes and relocations such as Figure 3 and Table 4. The document's visual design is otherwise stable.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the evaluation with a nonlinear hidden-state comparator and a joint-training analysis, improves reproducibility documentation, and corrects Table 2's inconsistent value. These are useful but bounded gains. Combined training shows mixed performance across tasks and metrics and does not resolve zero-shot transfer limitations; the central method and findings remain unchanged.
